依存図で辺でつながる区切りどうしを寄せて並べる

## 変更

依存図で、辺でつながる window の区切りが左右の両端に分かれ、線が間の区切りの上を長く横切る配置を直す。

- dagre の並べ替えは辺の交差の数だけを見るので、交差の数が同じ並びのうち、つながる区切りを互いに遠い端へ置いた並びに留まることがあった
- `transposeOrder` の後に `swapBlocks` を足した。同じ親の隣り合う 2 つの子 (枠なら中身と境界ごと) を全部の段で入れ替え、交差の数を増やさずに辺の order の差の和が減るあいだ続ける
- 子の左右の順が段によって食い違う親は扱わない。枠の中身が左右の境界の間に続いて並ぶ前提を保つため
- 交差の数か長さが厳密に減るときだけ入れ替えるので、今の並びが最良の図は動かない

## 検証

- `layout.test.js` に実データの並びを写した fixture を足した。区切り gh の a から隣の段の区切り uc の u へ辺が出る形で、gh と uc の間にほかの区切りを挟まないことを確かめる
- 寄せた区切りどうしの矩形が重ならないことを別のテストで確かめる (段を共有しない区切りが上下に積まれるため)
- 手元の実データ (`agents-daemon deps`) を node で配置し直すと、a→u の線の横の長さが約 1200px から約 380px に縮み、図の幅が 1717px から 1369px になった。区切りの矩形の重なりは無い
- `task gui:install` で建てたアプリを今の実データで開き、図が描かれ、枠どうしが重ならず、端へ寄って線が伸びたカードが無いことを見た。この時点の実データには対象の辺が無く、直した形そのものは fixture と上の配置し直しで確かめた

fix(server): Gori exchanges every Magic Pop result card in one talk

## Summary

Gori (the Magic Pop exchange operator) now exchanges every Magic Pop result card in the bag in one talk. Before, he took only the card in the lowest bag slot, so a player with several win or loss cards had to talk to him once per card.

This is native behaviour. The v1.188 server's exchange walks the whole bag from slot 13 and redeems each win and loss voucher in turn. It stops only when a reward cannot be granted, then answers code 5 and keeps the cards it already paid. No flag: the old one-card rule was a port defect. It applies to the v1.150 machine and to any later table alike.

- `apps/server/internal/game/action/gacha.go`
  - `HandleGachaExchange` loops over the voucher slots in slot order instead of picking the lowest one.
  - `gachaVoucherSlots` (new) lists the bag slots holding a win or loss voucher with its recorded pair, sorted.
  - `redeemGachaVoucher` (new) is the old single-card body, unchanged in what it pays. It reports whether a failure means "pass this card by" or "the grant failed".
  - A card the exchange cannot pay (a stacked row, a pair that is not an enabled prize row, an unresolved reward) is passed by, as the native loop passes slots it does not handle. Before, that card failed the whole request.
  - A failed grant stops the walk and appends the native `0xB1BE` refusal (code 5) after the frames already earned.
- `apps/server/internal/game/action/gacha_test.go`
  - `TestGachaExchangeRedeemsEveryVoucherInOneTalk` replaces `TestGachaExchangeTakesTheLowestSlotVoucherFirst`: a win in slot 13 and a loss in slot 20 are both paid by one request, slot 13 first.
  - `TestGachaExchangePassesByAVoucherItCannotPay`: a card with an invalid pair stays in the bag and the next voucher is still paid.

Each card's frames are the same as before (the `0x3645` quantity-zero update first, then the grant), one set per card, so the client's `UIIT_MSG_GACHA_EXCHANGE` line appears once per card.

## Player note

Player-note: Items: Gori now exchanges all your Magic POP result cards in one talk.

## Old tab

Old-tab: safe - the same item-update frames as before, one set per card; no new opcode

## Evidence

- [x] rg: blast radius pasted

```
$ rg -n 'HandleGachaExchange\(|gachaVoucherSlots\(|redeemGachaVoucher\(' apps/server
apps/server/internal/game/action/gacha.go:199:          frames, refusal := rt.HandleGachaExchange(divisionID, character, payload)   (0x71BE hub handler)
apps/server/internal/game/action/gacha.go:  HandleGachaExchange -> gachaVoucherSlots, redeemGachaVoucher (their only callers)
apps/server/internal/game/action/gacha_test.go: the exchange tests
```

- [x] callers: every caller and test of each changed function mapped. `HandleGachaExchange` has one production caller (the `0x71BE` handler) and the exchange tests; the two new helpers are called only from it.
- [x] edge cases: mapped, each with a test or a reason
  - Several vouchers in one bag: `TestGachaExchangeRedeemsEveryVoucherInOneTalk`.
  - A card that cannot be paid among good ones: `TestGachaExchangePassesByAVoucherItCannotPay`.
  - No voucher at all: still refused with code 5 (the existing tests).
  - A grant that fails part-way: not reachable with the shipped tables, so no test. Each card frees its own slot before its reward is planned, so a single reward row always fits. The code path keeps the cards already paid and answers 5, as the native loop does.
- [ ] native client: n/a - the client sends `0x71BE` once and prints one exchange line per item update; neither changes
- [x] native server: traced in the v1.188 server binary
- [x] subs: no unlabelled subs left in what was read

## Native claims

Server: `SR_GameServer.exe` v1.188, the repo-pinned build `bec2375e2c4c1073e3bf7761571470c430de251de74b452dbb86537348ef5290`. It was read through a capstone disassembly cache of the code-identical repack (`0efe7eaf…5e35`; its addresses match the pinned build's citations). The full trail is in `research/findings/magic-pop-biiv-server-v1188.md`, section "Gori's exchange takes every result card in one talk".

fix(server): Floor 6 stage monsters nested elsewhere keep their tactics (#4817)

Fixes #4817.

Old-tab: safe - server-only monster AI; no packet or client contract changes.

## What it fixes

The Qin-Shi tomb chain (SRO_QINSHI_TOMB) spawns Floor 6's stages at fixed points. Several stage codenames have no Floor 6 nest: the South clones (`MOB_TQ_SNAKEGENERAL_CLON`, `_CLON2`, `_CLON3`) and 14 of the West crowd's 15. The chain gave them a bare pinned point, which resolves to the generic wander contract. The generals stood passive where the original has them aggressive with sight 200.

The v1.188 server's wave spawn (`CTriggeredWaveSpawner` executing a MobShower entry) creates each monster through its spawn-tactics selection by ref. The tomb's tactics carry one normal row per object, shared by all of that codename's nests. So `tombChainSpawnerNest` now falls back, for a point spawner, to the codename's tomb nest on another floor: its AI fields at the stage point. A codename with no tomb nest at all keeps the wander contract.

## Native claims

| Claim | Evidence | How checked | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A wave entry's monster is created with tactics selected by its ref and rarity | v1.188 server: wave entry execute -> random-region spawn -> spawn-tactics selection -> spawn instance | BN, server (HLIL of the chain) | confirmed |
| One normal tactics row per tomb object (generals AggressType 0, sight 200; the West crowd AggressType 1, sight 100, aggressive champion rows) | `monster/data/qinshi_tomb_tactics.json` grouped by ObjectID | read | confirmed |
| The research note's "every spawner monster is aggressive" holds for the generals, not the West crowd's normal rows | the same tactics rows | read | corrected here; the West crowd stays passive |

## Verification

- `TestTombWaveSpawnTakesItsCodenamesTactics`: a South clone nested only on floor 3 spawns at the South point with that nest's aggression and sight; a clone with no nest keeps the pinned wander contract. Against main's `tomb_chain.go` it fails ("spawned with nest {... X:-17 ...}, want the floor 3 tactics").
- `pnpm task check:server:changed`: PASS.

None.

+/*
+================
+TestTombWaveSpawnTakesItsCodenamesTactics
+
+A Floor 6 stage codename nested only on another floor spawns at the
+stage point with that nest's tactics (the server picks a wave
+monster's tactics by its ref, #4817); one with no tomb nest at all
+keeps the pinned wander contract.

+func TestTombWaveSpawnTakesItsCodenamesTactics(t *testing.T) {
+	const general, floor3 = "MOB_TQ_SNAKEGENERAL_CLON", uint16(0x8005)
+	ids := tombFloor6Refs()
+	refs := map[uint32]monster.MonsterRef{
+		tombRefEast:  tombChainRef(tombRefEast, "MOB_TQ_EASTGUARDIAN"),
+		tombRefSouth: tombChainRef(tombRefSouth, "MOB_TQ_SOUTHGUARDIAN"),
+		tombRefWest:  tombChainRef(tombRefWest, "MOB_TQ_WESTGUARDIAN"),
+		tombRefNorth: tombChainRef(tombRefNorth, "MOB_TQ_NORTHGUARDIAN"),
+		tombRefFlame: tombChainRef(tombRefFlame, "MOB_TQ_FLAMEMASTER"),
+	}
+	for codename, id := range ids {
+		refs[id] = tombChainRef(id, codename)
+	}
+	elsewhere := tombChainNest(ids[general], 900)
+	elsewhere.RegionID = floor3
+	elsewhere.Aggressive, elsewhere.SightRange = true, 200
+	nests := []monster.NestRow{
+		tombChainNest(tombRefEast, 100), tombChainNest(tombRefSouth, 200), tombChainNest(tombRefWest, 300),
+		tombChainNest(tombRefNorth, 400), tombChainNest(tombRefFlame, 500), elsewhere,
+	}
+	s := NewMonsterState(monster.TemplateFromParts(refs, nests))
+	s.SetTimeSource(func() time.Time { return tombChainBase })
+	s.SetRandomSource(constantWord(16384))
+	if err := s.InstallTombChain(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("InstallTombChain: %v", err)
+	}
+	s.StartDivision("division")
+	tombAdvance(s, 1000)
+	var found, bare bool
+	for _, in := range s.InstancesInRegions("division", []uint16{0x8002}) {
+		switch in.Ref.Codename {
+		case general:
+			found = true
+			if !in.Nest.Aggressive || in.Nest.SightRange != 200 || in.Nest.RegionID != 0x8002 || in.Nest.X != -17 {
+				t.Fatalf("%s spawned with nest %+v, want the floor 3 tactics at the South point", general, in.Nest.SpawnPoint)
+			}
+		case "MOB_TQ_SNAKEGENERAL_CLON2":
+			bare = true
+			if in.Nest.Aggressive || !in.Nest.PolicyPinned {
+				t.Fatal("a codename with no tomb nest took tactics from nowhere")
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	if !found || !bare {
+		t.Fatalf("South stage not spawned (general %v, clone 2 %v)", found, bare)
+	}

fix(server): Floor 5's exits lead where the drawn portal order stands them (#4814)

Fixes #4814.

Old-tab: safe - server-only; the walk-in teleport frames are unchanged, only which Floor 6 arrival a Floor 5 exit picks.

## What it fixes

On Floor 5 of the Qin-Shi tomb (SRO_QINSHI_TOMB), the Flame Master's death opens three portals down to Floor 6's East, South and West arrivals. The v1.188 server stands them at the three exit places in one of six orders, drawn by `rand() % 6` when the floor is set up, so a party cannot learn which exit leads where. The port always used the first order.

- `simulation/tomb_chain.go`: `tombFloor5Orders` (the server's six-row table), a draw in `armFloorLocked` for the floor that raises the Floor 6 entry gate (each arm and re-arm), and `MonsterState.TombFloor5Destination(division, place)`.
- `action/walkin.go`: the exit zones map to their place; an open exit's link target becomes the arrival the chain names (`tombFloor6Arrivals`, teleportdata 139 / 141 / 140).

SRP: the chain owns the drawn state, the walk-in owns the zone-to-row mapping. No new copy of the order exists.

## Native claims

| Claim | Evidence | How checked | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Three portals, places (1498, 59, 1650) / (1815, 68, -1334) / (-1349, 68, 1101), arrivals East (7086, 140, 73) / South (69, 140, -7092) / West (-7089, 140, -71) | v1.188 server Floor 5 trigger setup: the place table and the three PortalSpawner entries | BN, server (HLIL and the table bytes) | confirmed |
| One `rand() % 6` picks the order from the six-row table {0,1,2} {0,2,1} {1,0,2} {1,2,0} {2,0,1} {2,1,0} | same function, one rand call indexing the table for all three entries | BN, server | confirmed |
| The draw happens per setup; the port draws per arm (the port's stand-in for the copy's setup) | the chain header's re-arm inference (#2372) | inferred, comment in `tomb_chain.go` | inferred |

## Verification

- `TestTombFloor5PortalsStandInTheDrawnOrder`: all six draws map each place to the expected arrival; no order before arming; a fourth place answers nothing.
- `TestFloor6WalkInWaitsForTheFlameMaster` now checks the arrival point. The mutant that drops the remap fails it ("arrived at x 7086, want 69").
- `pnpm task check:server:changed`: PASS (build, gofmt, vet, golangci-lint, tests of the two packages, gates). Its game-data tests skip on the stale shared data, so I ran the walk-in test directly: PASS (`-v`).
- `check:server-citations`: clean.
